coverageNote: Audited all 39 current Markdown source files under .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/12-release-distribution/ as 7 units. Each file received 3a implementer simulation, 3b Vision Rubric scoring, and 3c devil's-advocate probing; no prior audit artifact was read.

findings.claim: Active open questions identify an owner and a deferred pipeline stage, but omit both a deadline and the decision that each question blocks.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose hard versus soft delivery gating without a time-bound owner decision or an explicit downstream decision boundary.
findings.failureScenario: One delivery path blocks a time-critical release while another permits an override, producing incompatible provenance and release behavior.

findings.claim: Active open questions have no deadline or decision-blocked field; Deferred To names a stage, not either required datum.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must select direct delivery or an aggregator model before the owner has a deadline or a stated decision boundary.
findings.failureScenario: The system is built around partner contracts and DDEX certification when the product later chooses one aggregator integration, or vice versa.

findings.claim: Active open questions include owner and deferred stage only; they do not name a deadline or the decision blocked.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose webhook, polling, or public-store reconciliation without a time-bound owner decision.
findings.failureScenario: A store is shown as live or overdue from the wrong signal and the product either misses silent failures or relies on unsupported scraping.

findings.claim: Active open questions use Owner and Deferred To but provide neither a deadline nor a decision-blocked field.

evidence.excerpt: Is the rollout plan a **12-native object**

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether release planning owns tasks or delegates them to a generic project system without a time-bound decision.
findings.failureScenario: The product creates duplicate task systems or omits release-aware deadlines because the ownership model was guessed.

findings.claim: Active open questions lack the rubric-required deadline and explicit decision blocked; a deferred pipeline stage is the only routing data.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether a split dispute removes a release or only freezes payment without a time-bound owner choice.
findings.failureScenario: A legitimate release is taken down unnecessarily, or disputed revenue continues paying out, depending on which team implements the missing policy.

findings.claim: Active open questions have no deadline and no decision-blocked field, despite governing whether the platform claims against its own users.

evidence.excerpt: Does WeJammin claim against its own fans?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must select the claiming posture for fan videos without a time-bound owner decision or an explicit downstream decision boundary.
findings.failureScenario: The platform either monetizes fan videos without a values decision or silently forgoes claims that the product later expects to collect.

findings.claim: The root domain question register has no deadline or decision-blocked field for active domain decisions.

evidence.excerpt: Direct DSP delivery or via an aggregator?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must commit the domain to direct partner delivery or an aggregator path before the owner has a deadline or named blocked decision.
findings.failureScenario: The root architecture is sized for the wrong commercial delivery model, cascading incompatible integration and operational assumptions into every child.

findings.claim: Required platform-admin work has no settled actor or permission model: the domain calls the admin lens pending while child behavior lets that actor author, certify, and audit partner profiles.

evidence.excerpt: Admin authors PC-01..PC-13 from the partner

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent who can author, certify, second-review, and conflict-audit partner profiles, including authorization and separation-of-interest rules.
findings.failureScenario: A release-affecting profile change is made by an unauthorized or self-interested actor, with no defined access boundary or review responsibility.

findings.claim: The Release Builder cross-cut retains unresolved or obsolete behavior that conflicts with child specifications, so it cannot provide one implementable contract for delivery gating.

evidence.excerpt: Unresolved: whether a rule-pack update can invalidate
Release falls back to **Blocked on the affected store only**
**Not unfixable** — this is what per-target scoping is for

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether ownership-copy divergence blocks delivery, whether post-gate rule changes re-block a target, and whether an absent producer makes the release terminal.
findings.failureScenario: Different delivery paths apply contradictory gate outcomes, either blocking a releasable target or shipping an ownership assertion the system has marked unresolved.

findings.claim: The Store Management cross-cut leaves notification fan-out and rights-drift handling pending although the child specs supply different concrete behavior.

evidence.excerpt: Whether they notify the Producer is unresolved
the owning entity's members **and** to credited Producers.
Derivation is **re-evaluated on every 09/11 rights-record change event**

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose producer notification policy and whether a live rights-scope change auto-withdraws, alerts, or waits for artist action.
findings.failureScenario: Producers miss the only status summary or a release is silently removed after rights drift despite the owning selection flow requiring notification and an artist-controlled route.

findings.claim: No finalized fan-notification policy exists for a material release-date change: the cross-cut only records a leaning and an informal handoff to domains 20/21.

evidence.excerpt: Should a date move notify pre-saving fans?
Leaning: 12 surfaces the fact to the artist; 20/21 own any fan-facing message.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether to send fan notification, who authorizes it, and which domain owns the message after a date change.
findings.failureScenario: Fans are told before the artist announces the delay, or receive no actionable notice after their pre-save becomes invalid.

findings.claim: Suspension blocks all updates while the cross-cut identifies claim-resolving credits and clearances as updates; no final exception, authorization rule, or resolved route exists.

evidence.excerpt: the fix that would resolve the claim is often an update
The unresolved question is whether a **claim-resolving** update is exempt

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose between a total update freeze and a narrowly authorized claim-evidence path, including which actor can submit it and what it may mutate.
findings.failureScenario: A valid clearance or missing credit cannot be supplied to resolve a suspension, or an artist uses a broadly defined exception to alter the facts under a claim.

findings.claim: The update-to-redelivery flow recognizes that failure between takedown and re-delivery is its worst outcome but leaves recovery pending.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent compensation, retry, and user-visible state when a destructive takedown succeeds but the successor delivery fails.
findings.failureScenario: A live release is removed successfully and never restored, while the product has no specified recovery owner, retry boundary, or truthful state for the artist.

findings.claim: An ownership conflict on one UGC platform has no settled containment policy for registrations on other platforms.

evidence.excerpt: an unresolved conflict should suspend or prevent registration of the same audio elsewhere
Whether that is enforceable per-platform is unknown.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether to halt all remaining registrations, continue platform by platform, or create a conditional hold after the ownership assertion becomes contested.
findings.failureScenario: The platform continues asserting disputed ownership and creates new automated claims against third parties, or over-blocks unaffected rights platforms without an approved policy.

findings.claim: The derived whitelist has no reconciliation policy when its identity or credit sources change after registration.

evidence.excerpt: whitelist so it does not recur.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether a new contributor or changed band membership automatically changes a live whitelist, creates a review task, or leaves prior claim behavior unchanged.
findings.failureScenario: A newly credited collaborator is automatically claimed despite the product knowing the relationship, or a live whitelist changes without artist review and suppresses intended claims.
